items.title: Finalize the Tier-C threat model + key-management decision doc
items.context: docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md: trust anchor (pinned manifest, verify-against-pinned-not-self), independence definition + honest ceiling (cross-vendor, same-operator), the fail-closed rule table (which become the M1/M2 RED tests), and key gen/pin/rotate/revoke.

happy.desc: Doc contains a pinned-key trust anchor section: verdicts are verified against the PINNED manifest key for the claimed hostId, never the self-reported key in the bundle — reviewer confirms this is stated unambiguously
Independence definition section states cross-vendor (Claude vs Codex, distinct model families and keys) but same-operator ceiling, with allowed vs forbidden paper wording spelled out explicitly

Fail-closed rule table covers all 6 attack vectors: forged verdict, same-key masquerade, stale materialHash, replay, omission, key compromise — each row names detection mechanism and fail-closed response
Key lifecycle section covers generation, pinning, rotation, and revocation procedures as separate subsections with concrete steps
Doc has its own Section 6 acceptance checklist and a reader can derive every fail-closed rule and the independence boundary without external context
Doc references the code-verified current state: CLI-only chain (no Authority server), Ed25519 sign/verify, quorum evaluator in receipt-bundle.ts, decision-doc-quorum.ts, verdicts.ts

edge.desc: Independence ceiling section explicitly distinguishes what the paper MAY claim (cross-vendor independence) vs what it MUST NOT claim (mutually-distrusting multi-party) — the boundary is unambiguous with concrete forbidden phrases listed
Fail-closed table entries are derivable as M1/M2 RED tests: each row names a concrete attack scenario that can be implemented as a test without requiring further threat-model interpretation
Key rotation procedure addresses the transition window where both old and new keys must be valid, and revocation addresses delayed discovery of compromise (not just immediate revocation)
Trust anchor section addresses the bootstrap problem: how the initial pinned manifest is established and by whom, and what happens if the manifest itself is corrupted

adversarial.desc: Doc does NOT contain over-claimed independence wording: phrases like mutually-distrusting parties, fully independent hosts, zero-trust multi-party, or trustless multi-party are absent — grep for these exact phrases must return zero matches

Doc does NOT assume a central Authority server exists for signing or reconciliation — the server is deprecated and the chain is CLI-only; any reference to Authority must be historical or explicitly marked deprecated
Fail-closed table does NOT have a catch-all pass-through, allow-by-default, or best-effort entry — every unrecognized or unhandled case must fail closed
Key compromise row does NOT assume compromise is detectable in real-time — must address the delayed-discovery case where a key was compromised but the operator does not yet know

Doc does NOT conflate key independence (distinct Ed25519 keys) with model independence (distinct vendor/model families) — both are separately required for the cross-vendor claim and named as distinct conditions
